brief_summary: Three-row matrix pairing each wrist deviation a flat row-staggered keyboard forces (ulnar deviation, pronation, extension) with the single geometry that corrects it (split opening angle, tenting gable, zero/negative slope plus low profile). Left column carries a small line-drawn hand glyph with the deviated angle marked in the caution colour; right column carries a matching board glyph with the corrected posture marked in dusty rose. The numbers on the correction side are the ranges the article cites from Rempel 2007/2009 and the Glove80 spec.
data_sources: split-ergo-mechanics-deep-dive.mdx § 'Three deviations, three fixes' — 'Ulnar deviation is the sideways bend toward the pinky... Pronation is the forearm rotation that turns the palms to face the desk... Extension is the upward bend at the wrist'
split-ergo-mechanics-deep-dive.mdx § 'Three deviations, three fixes' — 'brought mean ulnar deviation from roughly 12 degrees to within 5 degrees of neutral' (Marklin and Simoneau, Human Factors 2000)
split-ergo-mechanics-deep-dive.mdx § 'Three deviations, three fixes' — 'a mid-range opening angle of about 15 degrees was the best trade' (Rempel 2009)

split-ergo-mechanics-deep-dive.mdx § 'How much of this is evidence-backed' — 'the 12-degree split, 14-degree gable, zero-slope configuration; the negative slope did best on pronation' and '0 or -7 degrees of slope' (Rempel 2007)
split-ergo-mechanics-deep-dive.mdx § 'Choc versus MX spacing' — 'lowest key sits 20 mm from the desk to the top of the keycap' (Glove80 technical specification)
